smart contract.definition: A smart contract is like a digital vending machine. Just as you put money in a vending machine and automatically get a snack, a smart contract automatically executes an agreement when certain conditions are met. On Stacks, these are written in Clarity language and run on top of Bitcoin's security.

proof of transfer.definition: Proof of Transfer (PoX) is Stacks' unique way of securing the network that's different from Bitcoin's Proof of Work. Instead of wasting energy like traditional mining, Stacks miners 'transfer' Bitcoin to STX holders who are 'Stacking' their tokens.

clarity language.definition: Clarity is Stacks' smart contract programming language, designed to be safer and more predictable than other blockchain languages like Solidity. It is 'decidable' - meaning you can predict what a contract will do before running it.

stx token.definition: STX is the native cryptocurrency of the Stacks network - think of it as the fuel that powers everything on Stacks. You use STX to pay for transaction fees, participate in smart contracts, and 'Stack' your tokens to earn Bitcoin rewards.

bitcoin finality.definition: Bitcoin finality means your transaction is permanently recorded and cannot be reversed - it has the highest level of security in crypto. On Stacks, transactions inherit this security from Bitcoin.

stacking.definition: Stacking is like earning interest on your STX tokens, but instead of getting more STX, you earn Bitcoin! You lock up your STX tokens for a certain period, and miners pay you Bitcoin for the right to mine Stacks blocks.

defi.definition: DeFi (Decentralized Finance) is like traditional banking, but without the banks. Instead of going to a bank for loans, savings, or trading, you interact directly with smart contracts on the blockchain.

dapp.definition: A dApp (decentralized application) is like a regular app, but instead of running on company servers, it runs on the blockchain. This means no single entity controls it - it's owned and operated by its users.

nft.definition: An NFT (Non-Fungible Token) is like a digital certificate of ownership for unique items. While anyone can copy a digital image, only one person can own the official NFT version.

web3.definition: Web3 is the vision of a new internet where users own their data and digital assets instead of big tech companies. It lets you truly own your digital stuff through blockchain technology.

bitcoin.definition: Bitcoin is the first and most secure cryptocurrency - often called 'digital gold.' It's a peer-to-peer electronic cash system that allows you to send money anywhere in the world without banks or governments.

blockchain.definition: A blockchain is like a digital ledger that's copied across thousands of computers worldwide. Every transaction is recorded in 'blocks' that are chained together cryptographically.
